submitter: deferred_work_item_park lane (bugs_open/396) — SITE-LOCK EXCEPTION, ROUND 2, resubmit of 175df761 (r1 REVISE; editquality read edit 1's fragment as being reused verbatim in edit 4)
rationale:
ROUND 2. r1's gating concern was that siteLockExceptionSQL()'s $1-scoped fragment would be dropped verbatim into find_dispatchable_site's config.query — a CROSS-SITE scan that joins `sites s` and has no $1 — and so could not work there. THE OBJECTION IS RIGHT ABOUT THE HAZARD AND WRONG ABOUT THE CODE, and I am fixing the thing it was right about rather than only correcting the record. Migration 633 never reuses the Go fragment: it spells the rule against the JOINED ALIAS — `WHERE (s.locked_at IS NULL OR wi.id = ANY(COALESCE(s.lock_except_item_ids, ARRAY[]::uuid[]))) AND wi.status IN` — with no $1 anywhere, and that exact text was dry-run against the live database inside a transaction that was then rolled back, with guards asserting the patched gate both NAMES the column and STILL CONTAINS its locked_at test. My r1 PLAN was ambiguous about this; the SQL was not.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE CODE FOR r2: a reviewer trying to merge the two spellings in their head is the tell that the next person to DRY them up will try it for real. So the divergence is now stated where it will be met — siteLockExceptionSQL()'s doc comment explains that the two SQL contexts are not the same context and that NO shared form is correct in both — and pinned by a fifth test, TestSiteLockExceptionSQLIsNotTheSelectorSpelling, which FAILS if the fragment is rewritten against a bare joined alias to 'match the selector'. Making them the same is now a build failure, not a judgement call.

Everything else in r1 stands and is unchanged. For the record, the r1 reviewers' own read-only checks VALIDATED the design's three load-bearing assumptions: exactly one active row per target agent (so the anchored config edit is unambiguous), `load_items` is a top-level workflow.steps key (so the jsonb_set path is right), and `config.query` is the anchor that exists.

bugs_open/396, REPLACING the park verb this lane submitted as ed821065. That round came back REVISE on a HIGH from prior_art_librarian, and the objection was right: I asserted "the platform offers NO verb for holding a site's work queue" without checking, and sites.locked_at / sites.locked_by already exist. I verified every part of the objection myself before acting on it - the columns exist, 3 of 51 sites are locked right now with a real reason in locked_by, build-pipeline-trigger>find_dispatchable_site gates on `s.locked_at IS NULL`, and there are admin lock/unlock endpoints. Crucially the lock MUTATES NO WORK-ITEM ROW: it strands nothing, holds no idx_swi_dedup slot, and the 22-day stall that motivated 396 could not have happened under it. Migration 621's park verb makes the WRONG tool tidier and is not the fix.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS NARROWER: the lock is all-or-nothing. `sites` has only locked_at and locked_by. That is exactly why the mortgagecalculator lane wrote a 15-second auto-defer backstop - its own handoff labels the site lock "(a)" and item status "(b) ITEM STATUS - the finer control" - and that backstop minted 38 of the 52 unattributable parked rows. Give the lock the exception list it lacks and the reason to reach for status='deferred' goes away. No work-item row changes status, so nothing can be stranded.

I BELIEVE THIS IS ARCHITECTURE-SCOPE AND AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN LETTING THE SEAT FIND IT. It changes what a shared dispatch gate GUARANTEES: today "a locked site dispatches nothing", after this "a locked site dispatches nothing unless items are explicitly excepted". Per the 2026-07-29 ruling that is the RFC trigger, not the additive-and-inert case. It ships opt-in with the unsafe default OFF on BOTH axes (a NULL exception list, and honour_site_lock defaulting false), but I am not claiming RFC_022's narrowing, because migration 633 gives it a live consumer by design.

THE TRAP THAT SHAPED THE DESIGN, AND THE REASON THE FILES ARE SPLIT. find_dispatchable_site selects a SITE, not an item. The obvious one-clause fix - teaching that gate to select a locked site when one excepted item is dispatchable - would UNLOCK THE WHOLE SITE, because the very next step (build-dispatch-loop>load_items -> LoadWorkItemsAction) then loads every dispatchable item on it. That loader has NEVER checked sites.locked_at; the lock is enforced at exactly ONE gate today. So both halves are required, the binary must ship first, and the config half is a _HOLD file.

⚠ I misread this once already and the misreading is instructive: load_work_item_actions.go:134 DOES check the site lock, but it is inside WriteBuildItemsAction (minting new items), and its log line misnames itself as "LoadWorkItemsAction: site is locked, skipping". Do not take that log string as evidence of a second gate.

plan.summary: Give sites.locked_at the exception list it lacks, so "hold this site EXCEPT these N items" is expressible without moving any work item to a status it cannot leave. Three artefacts: a nullable uuid[] column (migration 632, inert on apply); a Go arm in LoadWorkItemsAction behind an opt-in step-config key honour_site_lock (default false, so the statement stays byte-identical for the two site-work-orchestrator callers that gate on nothing today); and a HELD config migration (633) that enables the key on the automated dispatch step AND adds the exception clause to find_dispatchable_site. 633 must not be applied before the binary carrying the Go arm has rolled - applied early it converts a full site hold into no hold at all. Four mutation-proven tests, each made to fail and the tree then restored byte-identically.

edits.rationale: The SQL fragment as a function, not an inline string, for the same reason refreshOpenWorkItemSQL is one: the test that pins its arms reads THE FRAGMENT THAT RUNS instead of re-deriving its own copy and agreeing with itself. ALSO (r2): r2 ONLY. Answers r1's gating objection in the code rather than in prose: the two spellings of the lock rule are deliberately different and a future tidy-up must be refused, not merely warned about.
edits.sketch:
func siteLockExceptionSQL() string — returns `AND ((SELECT s.locked_at FROM sites s WHERE s.id = $1) IS NULL OR wi.id = ANY(COALESCE((SELECT s.lock_except_item_ids FROM sites s WHERE s.id = $1), ARRAY[]::uuid[])))`. Both arms load-bearing: lose the locked_at arm and every UNLOCKED site stops yielding work fleet-wide; lose the COALESCE and a NULL exception list becomes a NULL comparison instead of meaning THE FULL HOLD. It binds only $1, deliberately, so it adds no placeholder and cannot shift the caller's argIdx bookkeeping for the pipeline/handler/limit filters appended after it.

r2 ADDITION: siteLockExceptionSQL()'s doc comment gains: ⚠⚠ DO NOT REUSE THIS FRAGMENT IN find_dispatchable_site — this one is per-site and PARAMETERISED ($1 already bound by the caller); the selector is a CROSS-SITE SCAN that joins `sites s` and has NO $1, and is spelled `WHERE (s.locked_at IS NULL OR wi.id = ANY(COALESCE(s.lock_except_item_ids, ARRAY[]::uuid[])))`. Dropping this fragment there references a $1 that does not exist and breaks site selection fleet-wide. Names council 175df761 as the evidence that a careful reader does try to merge them.

edits.rationale: The opt-in read and the append. Default OFF keeps the statement byte-identical for site-work-orchestrator's two load_work_items callers, which are human-initiated and gate on nothing today - changing that flow is a separate decision, not a side effect of this one.
edits.sketch: honourSiteLock, _ := config["honour_site_lock"].(bool); siteLockClause := ""; if honourSiteLock { siteLockClause = siteLockExceptionSQL() } ... query := `...` + siteLockClause — appended BEFORE the argIdx-numbered filters, which is why the fragment must not introduce a placeholder.

edits.rationale: The column, separate from the config half BECAUSE it is safe now: a nullable column nothing reads is inert by construction, so it can land before the roll while 633 waits.
edits.sketch: ALTER TABLE sites ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS lock_except_item_ids uuid[]; + COMMENT ON COLUMN stating that BOTH halves are required. DO/RAISE guards: the column exists and is an ARRAY; a NEGATIVE CONTROL that 0 existing rows carry a value (or the 'inert by construction' claim is false); and a POSITIVE CONTROL that at least one site is currently locked - without it the negative control passes just as well on a fleet where the mechanism this extends is not in use at all.

edits.rationale: Both config edits in ONE held file, because (a) without (b) is an unlock and (b) without (a) is inert - they must land together, after the binary.
edits.sketch: snapshot_agent() on both agents first. Anchored replace on build-pipeline-trigger>find_dispatchable_site config.query (⚠ config.query, NOT pre_query - the step is a query_database action; reading the wrong key is how a first draft patched nothing and reported success), guarded to ABORT if the anchor is absent, and to say 'already applied' if the query already names the column. Then jsonb_set honour_site_lock=true on build-dispatch-loop>load_items. GET DIAGNOSTICS asserts exactly 1 row each. Guards read back with a query the file does not contain and assert: the gate NAMES the column, the gate STILL CONTAINS its locked_at test (lose that and a locked site with no exceptions dispatches everything), the opt-in is true, and a NEGATIVE CONTROL that 0 site-work-orchestrator steps gained the key.

edits.rationale: Four tests written against the failure that would actually happen - an UNLOCK, not a strand. All four mutation-proven before submitting, then the tree restored byte-identically (verified with diff -q against copies taken before mutating). ALSO (r2): r2 ONLY. A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share (RFC_010 section 2's own reasoning), so the divergence is pinned by a test.
edits.sketch:
TestSiteLockExceptionSQLKeepsBothHalves (mutations: drop the locked_at arm -> FAILS; drop the COALESCE -> FAILS, both verified). TestSiteLockExceptionSQLBindsOnlyDollarOne - the quiet one that would cost an incident, because the fragment is appended BEFORE the caller's $2/$3 filters and a stray placeholder makes every later one bind the wrong value (mutation: $1 -> $2 -> FAILS, verified). TestLoadWorkItemsActionIsOptInForTheSiteLock - ⚠ parses the AST with comments DROPPED, because a source scan would match the comment explaining the flag and pass even with the read deleted (mutation: hard-wire honourSiteLock := true -> FAILS, verified).

r2 ADDITION: TestSiteLockExceptionSQLIsNotTheSelectorSpelling asserts the fragment still looks the lock up through `FROM sites s WHERE s.id = $1`. MUTATION: rewrite it against a bare `s.locked_at` joined alias so it 'matches the selector' -> FAILS. LoadWorkItemsAction's FROM is `site_work_items wi` with no sites join, so the bare form does not compile there anyway — the test makes that a red build instead of a discovery.

edits.rationale: Registered in the SAME COMMIT that ships it (owner ruling 2026-07-28 condition 2), and WII-034 (the park verb) amended to point here as the preferred mechanism rather than left as a competing answer.
edits.sketch: New entry for the exception list: what, status, the ONE-GATE fact, the ordering constraint, and the explicit non-goal (it does not change site-work-orchestrator). WII-034 amended: the verb stays for the residual case but the site lock is the answer for holding a site, and a verb-park still holds the dedup slot and can be drained by an automated retraction without going through unpark.

grounded_in: r1 gating objection (editquality, corr 175df761): "siteLockExceptionSQL() is written as a $1-scoped fragment ... But edit 4 reuses the same framing for find_dispatchable_site's config.query, which is a cross-site scan that already joins `sites s` with no `$1` site-id parameter — the fragment as described cannot be dropped in verbatim there."

Migration 633's ACTUAL text, read back from the file: v_new_clause CONSTANT text := 'WHERE (s.locked_at IS NULL OR wi.id = ANY(COALESCE(s.lock_except_item_ids, ARRAY[]::uuid[]))) AND wi.status IN' — the joined alias, no $1. The fragment is NOT reused; r1's plan was ambiguous, the SQL was correct, and the concatenated 632+633 dry run with a final ROLLBACK passed every guard.

r1's own reviewer checks, which validated the design: build-dispatch-loop and build-pipeline-trigger have exactly ONE active row each; load_items IS a top-level workflow.steps key; config.query is present on find_dispatchable_site.

council ed821065, prior_art_librarian, HIGH: "Rationale's core premise — 'The platform offers NO verb for [holding a site's work queue]' — is contradicted by an existing mechanism already in the Schema: sites.locked_at / sites.locked_by." Verified first-hand: both columns exist; 3 of 51 sites locked as of 2026-08-25.

The live lock gate, read verbatim from agent_definitions: build-pipeline-trigger>find_dispatchable_site config.query = "SELECT wi.site_id::text, s.domain FROM site_work_items wi JOIN sites s ON s.id = wi.site_id WHERE s.locked_at IS NULL AND wi.status IN ('triaged','approved') ..."

LoadWorkItemsAction's own WHERE, read at HEAD: "FROM site_work_items wi WHERE wi.site_id = $1 AND wi.status IN ('triaged','approved') AND wi.attempt_count < wi.max_attempts AND <retry-not-pending> AND ..." — NO locked_at anywhere. The lock is enforced at exactly one gate.

⚠ load_work_item_actions.go:134 DOES check the lock but is inside WriteBuildItemsAction (declared :104), and its log line reads "LoadWorkItemsAction: site is locked, skipping". The log string misnames its own function and is how this lane misread the code the first time.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] every live consumer of the load_work_items action, recursive walk over agent_definitions: build-dispatch-loop>load_items (max_items 5), site-work-orchestrator>load_work_items (20), site-work-orchestrator>load_fix_items (20). Only the first is opted in by 633; no scheduled_task drives site-work-orchestrator, so that flow is human-initiated.

mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption/HANDOFF_2026-08-03_continue_here.md:81-90 — the backstop that made 38 of the unattributable rows, and its own framing: the site lock is "(a)", item status is "(b) ITEM STATUS — the finer control", with the comment "'deferred' is NOT in workItemTerminalStatuses, so the row keeps its idx_swi_dedup slot and release is one UPDATE". They knew about the slot and treated it as a feature.

[MEASURED 2026-08-25] the sites currently locked, with their reasons from locked_by: adversecreditmortgage.co.uk ("portfolio_positioning: owner HALT 2026-08-18 pending classifier register-input (RFC) + builder-flow decision"), indoorplanters.co.uk and buytoletcalculator.uk (brief-writer tests, "LOCKED so nothing can build").

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 (RFC_010 §2): new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field whose UNSAFE default is OFF, set on the CALLER so a reviewer of the caller sees it. Applied on both axes here: NULL exception list, and honour_site_lock default false set in migration 633 on build-dispatch-loop>load_items.

Owner ruling 2026-07-29 §1: an addition needs an RFC when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. This does — "a locked site dispatches nothing" becomes "...unless items are explicitly excepted" — which is why this submission declares itself architecture-scope rather than claiming RFC_022's opt-in narrowing (633 gives the key a live consumer by design, so condition 3 of that narrowing fails).
Owner ruling 2026-07-28 condition (2): the seam is registered in the SAME COMMIT that ships it — hence the register edit in this plan.

Migration 575's precedent for the _HOLD pattern: a config key must not go live before the binary that reads it, or the fix looks live when it is not. Here the failure is worse than inert — applied early, 633 converts a full site hold into no hold at all on exactly the sites somebody deliberately locked.

Dry-run evidence: 632 and 633 were concatenated into one transaction and run against the live database with a final ROLLBACK. All guards passed, including 633's four read-backs (gate names the column; gate KEEPS its locked_at test; opt-in true; 0 site-work-orchestrator steps touched) and 632's positive control (3 sites locked). Verified after: the column is absent and the gate is unpatched, so the rollback left nothing behind.

All four Go tests mutation-proven before submission and the tree restored byte-identically afterwards (diff -q against pre-mutation copies): drop the locked_at arm -> FAIL; drop the COALESCE -> FAIL; shift $1 to $2 -> FAIL; hard-wire the opt-in to true -> FAIL.

work_item_retraction.go:205 counts `parked += n` when it closes a `deferred` row — so an automated retraction can release a deliberate park without going through any unpark route. That is a second reason the lock (which touches no row) is the better mechanism than the park verb, and it was raised as a medium objection on ed821065.
